works.author: Kreutzer, Rodolphe

works.notes: Sustained long-bow legato; swells and tone control

works.title: Étude No. 2 in C major

works.contents: Allegro moderato; the basic détaché study with many bow-stroke variants, string crossings and intonation (sequences of broken-chord figures)
works.notes: Core détaché study: bow strokes, string crossings, intonation

works.title: Étude No. 3 in C major

works.contents: Allegro moderato; left-hand sequences: shifting by seconds, many fourths, climbing to the high positions; bow demands moderate (strokes of No. 2)
works.notes: Shifting sequences and fourths; left hand leads, bow moderate
works.edition: Magasin de Musique, Paris, 1805 (first ed., 40 studies; IMSLP); numbered as in Singer/Schirmer 1894 and Henle HN 1177

works.contents: No tempo word in IMSLP's list (Henle title: 'Étude du Staccato'); slurred staccato from the wrist, easy scales and arpeggios for the left hand
works.notes: Slurred staccato bowing from the wrist

works.title: Étude No. 5 in E-flat major

works.title: Étude No. 12 in A minor

works.author: Kreutzer, Rodolphe
works.title: Étude No. 13 in A major

works.notes: Bariolage and chord arpeggios; held fingers; flexible wrist
works.edition: Not in the 1805 first edition: comes from Kreutzer's revised edition (J. Frey, Paris, c.1822-24, per Henle) and was first combined with the original 40 in Rolla's 42-study edition (1830s, probably); numbered as in Singer/Schirmer and Henle HN 1177

note: NUMBERING: all 42 use the standard numbering of Singer/Schirmer (1894), Henle HN 1177, RCM and Wikipedia. IMSLP's work-info list is in the older 40-study numbering (without the added bariolage and broken-octave studies), so IMSLP no. n = no. n for n<=12, n+1 for 13-23, n+2 for 24-40. Nos. 13 and 25 are not in the 1805 first edition (Henle preface); they come from Kreutzer's revised edition (c.1822-24) and entered the 42 via Rolla (1830s). The often-quoted date 1796 is an error for the first edition (1805); 1794 and 1796 were two smaller sets of 6 and 12 studies. KEYS: en/fr Wikipedia and Henle agree on all 42; IMSLP (mapped from its 40-study numbering) agrees on 38 of its 40 and lacks Nos. 13 and 25. IMSLP differs on No. 21 (B minor per Henle/Wikipedia/Naxos, D major per IMSLP and Cutter; same two-sharp signature) and No. 24 (G minor per Wikipedia/Henle, B-flat major per IMSLP; same signature). Both are confidence 'medium' and explained in `contents`. Tempo words differ in places (Henle: No. 28 Andante, 31 Allegro, 36 Allegro, 41 Andante); noted in `contents`. LEVELS: base is the RCM 2021 syllabus mapped to the catalogue scale (RCM 6 = 2, 7 = 3, 8 = 4, 9 = 5, 10 = 6). RCM names Nos. 2-17 individually and gives pools for 18-26 (RCM 9) and 27-42 (RCM 10); the 2013 RCM etude book agrees for Nos. 2, 4, 11, 12. Adjusted by hand: No. 5 up one (RCM 4 is an outlier, printed 'play Violin 1 only'), Nos. 4 and 6 up one (staccato; needs all positions, per Cutter and Somerville), No. 1 set at 4 (not on RCM lists; teachers place it after the trill studies). Henle's per-study rating (2-5) is quoted in `exams` but not used to adjust levels. The median study sits at RCM 9 = level 5, which supports the existing book level. NOT AVAILABLE: ASTA CAP handbook (members only), ABRSM ARSM list and AMEB manual (abrsm.org and ameb.edu.au returned HTTP 403 to my fetches; AMEB grade books list an unnumbered 'Etude (Kreutzer)'), Trinity, NYSSMA and UIL lists. So there are no ASTA, ABRSM, AMEB or Trinity placements by study number. WELL_KNOWN: true for the studies named in the brief (2, 8, 9, 13, 14, 19, 35) plus those RCM prints in its own etude books or names in both RCM editions (3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 15). Nos. 19 and 35 rest on the brief only (no document found). Others (e.g. 1, 10, 16, 17, 23, 24, 29, 31, 42) may be commonly assigned too, but I found no documentary evidence. DESCRIPTIONS follow Cutter (1903), Somerville (1924), Henle's labels and the Wikipedia incipits. METHOD: read-only; pages fetched with WebFetch/curl, the fetch tool cached a few PDFs (RCM syllabus, Henle preface) in its own results folder and I read them with the system pdftotext; nothing installed, no score downloaded. EXTRA WORKS: (1) 'Études des diverses positions et démanchés' is an undated 7-page André print attributed to Kreutzer (IMSLP, e-rara, RISM A/I K 2431); its contents and level are unchecked (confidence low) and the category is a judgement from the title. (2) Massart's 'L'Art de travailler les études de Kreutzer' (Leduc 1893, 412 fingering/bowing examples) is listed here because the French-school researcher (franco_b) left it to the Kreutzer slice; its level is an estimate and its contents were not inspected.
